claims.claim: B is an interviewee who has had an interview

evidence.quote: thank the interviewer again for the opportunity of the interview

claims.adjudication_reason: A addresses B as 'you' throughout and instructs B to thank 'the interviewer' and 'say goodbye to the interviewer before you leave,' strongly presupposing B occupies the interviewee role. The interview is described as ongoing (turn 1: 'when the interview finally comes to an end'), so 'who has had an interview' is slightly imprecise but the core claim (B is an interviewee) is well-grounded.

claims.claim: B has thanked the interviewer at least once prior to this moment
claims.attribute: B previously expressed thanks to the interviewer
claims.adjudication_reason: 'Thank the interviewer again' contains the presupposition trigger 'again,' which logically requires that a prior thanking event occurred. This is a direct semantic presupposition.

claims.claim: B is expected to receive a reply regarding the interview
claims.attribute: B will receive a reply about the interview outcome

evidence.quote: ask when you can receive a reply

claims.adjudication_reason: Turn 5 ('ask when you can receive a reply') and turn 9 ('the reply you get') both presuppose that B will receive a reply. 'The reply you get' uses a definite NP with a relative clause, entailing existence of a future reply for B.

claims.claim: B is currently at the interview location with the interviewer present
claims.attribute: B is at the interview site before leaving

evidence.quote: say goodbye to the interviewer before you leave

claims.adjudication_reason: Turn 11 instructs B to 'say goodbye to the interviewer before you leave,' which presupposes B is currently at a location with the interviewer present and is about to leave. This is a necessary inference from the spatial deixis in the instruction.

claims.claim: B is expected to leave after the interview
claims.attribute: B will leave the interview location
claims.adjudication_reason: Turn 11 'before you leave' directly presupposes that B will leave the current location after the interview. This is a straightforward temporal presupposition from the subordinate clause.

claims.claim: B was given an opportunity for the interview

evidence.quote: thank the interviewer again for the opportunity of the interview

claims.adjudication_reason: Turn 3 'thank the interviewer again for the opportunity of the interview' contains the definite NP 'the opportunity of the interview,' which presupposes that an opportunity was given to B. This is a clear existential presupposition.

claims.claim: The interview has been ongoing and is nearing its end

evidence.quote: When the interview finally comes to an end

claims.adjudication_reason: Turn 1 'When the interview finally comes to an end' presupposes the interview is currently ongoing (it hasn't ended yet) and that it is approaching its conclusion ('finally' implies duration and anticipation of the end). This is a direct temporal presupposition.
